expectations.text: The reply begins with a progress marker identifying Phase 1.
expectations.evidence: **Phase 1 of 5 · Explore and choose a direction**

expectations.text: The reply includes a briefing with four labeled sections covering key debates, major voices, patterns, and open questions.
expectations.evidence: The briefing has four labeled sections: "**Key debates**", "**Major voices**", "**Patterns**" and "**Open questions**".

expectations.text: The briefing is roughly 300 to 500 words long (it fails if under 250 or over 600 words).
expectations.evidence: Counting the four sections gives roughly 380–400 words, which is inside the 300–500 range.

expectations.text: The reply presents a mind map, either as an HTML page built from the skill's mind map template or as an indented text tree.
expectations.evidence: "I saved an interactive map of six possible angles at .../mind-map.html". The tool log shows the HTML was built from templates/mind-map.html by replacing __MIND_MAP_DATA__.

expectations.text: The mind map has 4 to 6 top-level angles, each with 2 or 3 narrower angles, and every angle has a saturation value between 0 and 1 (or, for a text tree, a crowdedness label).
expectations.evidence: The reply says there are "six possible angles". Every branch shown has 2 or 3 children (for example, Student achievement has 3 and Teachers has 2). Every angle shown has a saturation value between 0 and 1 (for example, "saturation": 0.85). The file excerpt is cut off, so the last branches could not be checked.

expectations.text: No mind map label is phrased as a research question; labels are short topics.
expectations.evidence: The labels are short topics, for example "Student achievement", "Budgets and cost savings" and "Districts that switched back". None is phrased as a question.

expectations.text: The reply does not tell the user which angle they should choose or which one is best.
expectations.evidence: "Take some time with the map, then tell me: which direction pulls you in". The reply recommends no angle.

expectations.text: Every link or DOI that appears in the reply or the mind map points to a page the transcript shows Claude opened (fetched) during this session.
expectations.evidence: Every link visible in the reply and the map was fetched this session: k12dive, edweek, chalkbeat and ncsl. The map excerpt is cut off, so any links after that point could not be checked.

expectations.text: The reply asks the user which direction interests them and why.
expectations.evidence: "which direction pulls you in, and why that one rather than the others?"

expectations.text: The reply asks the user no more than two questions.
expectations.evidence: The reply asks only one compound question, about which direction and why. "You can also ask me how I know..." is an offer, not a question.
